lesson_title: The Hydrosphere: Tablespoons From a Twenty-Litre Bucket
hook_text: Pour EVERY drop of water on Earth into one twenty-litre bucket. Your share to drink? A few tablespoons.
clip_script: Imagine every drop of water the Earth owns poured into a single twenty-litre bucket. All of it: oceans, ice caps, rivers, clouds, the water under the ground and the water inside every living body. Now inspect your stock. Just over nineteen litres of the bucket is sea water — salty, undrinkable, useless on a farm. Scoop out the fresh water and most of THAT is ice, locked away at the poles. What is left — the fresh, liquid, reachable water that every tap, farm, elephant and maize plant on land must divide — comes to a few tablespoons. Tablespoons, out of twenty litres. That is the hydrosphere: a soaked planet, and a civilisation surviving on the tablespoons.
visual_style: A giant bucket filling with ocean blue, a thin white frozen layer skimmed off, then a tiny spoon lifting out the world's drinking share; cut to a drop's journey — ocean, cloud, mountain, borehole, tap.
mood: Awe flipping into urgency — abundance revealed as scarcity.
pacing: Slow fill, sharp reveal of the tablespoons, quick-cut journey of one drop, reflective close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow one drop through all four spheres of the planet.
